shots.notes: Good-looking cutaway coil with believable copper and fins. The casing-split reveal works. The mechanism is under-explained: the change from liquid to vapour is not drawn (for example cold blue liquid becoming vapour bubbles along the tube), and arrow directions flip between f270 and f313. By f313 the push-in cuts the coil off at the left edge. The lower ~45% of frame is empty wall. At f222 the removed front casing shows as a large slab at the top right, which is distracting. At f270 heat-arrow direction contradicts 'absorb' (semantic, not a render artifact).

shots.notes: The flow concept is clear: hot vapour runs through the wall to the outdoor unit and heat leaves to outside air. But the indoor-unit asset swap breaks continuity, and lighting is flat (no contact shadows under the outdoor unit legs, uniform sky). The floor has visible aliasing. Labels overlap the parts they name. The outdoor unit is cut at the right edge in f342/f373, and the indoor panel is cut at the left in f433. The caption box covers the outdoor unit's legs. The indoor-unit dark panel is a continuity/asset defect, and the label overlap is a composition defect; both are reflected in the scores.

reference_comparison.notes: REF-002 (How Come? desert video) has fully dressed, deep environments: sky, terrain, props and set dressing. It uses consistent stylized-realistic characters with costume detail, directional sun with long cast shadows, and physical props carrying the information (a dial thermometer at 40 C). Captions are minimal and float mid-frame. This render takes place against bare wall planes: S002-S004 are mostly empty wall or flat sky. The mannequin-limbed Bima and the crude macro hand are well below REF character quality. Explanation leans on UI pill labels and 2D arrow sprites rather than physical props. Lighting is soft but flat, with no strong key-light direction. Mechanism clarity in S002/S004 is reasonable and the story beats are understandable, which is why mechanism and story score 3.
